quote.text: Omne ignotum pro magnifico est.” — everything unknown is taken for magnificent.
quote.author: Tacitus, Agricola, chapter 30, in the speech he gives to Calgacus, about AD 98

stories.headline: Araghchi cuts Iran’s Hormuz reopening timeline from seven days to two
stories.dek: Qatar’s own gas carrier Al Mayeda was struck on 30 October, hours before its government’s third day of mediation; Washington has told Gulf allies to expect strikes as early as 4 November.

stories.headline: Meta and Microsoft raised US$62.5bn in one day, naming no use
stories.dek: Both prospectuses say “general corporate purposes”; neither names a data centre. Microsoft’s filing of 29 October left all ten coupons and maturities blank.

stories.headline: Police orders bar 124,617 Taiwanese from internet banking for five years
stories.dek: Fraud losses fell 28.9 per cent in September. The instrument is an administrative admonition, issued by a police agency without a trial, and about one per cent of appeals succeed.

stories.headline: Wilmar reports US$22.5m of sales to six companies served haze notices
stories.dek: Five of the ten firms had agreed to pay for their own investigators by 31 October, two more are willing, and three have not been named as agreeing at all.

stories.headline: Meze’s flagship driver is built by Rinaro, and the spec sheet says so
stories.dek: Spirit Torino publishes no price at all for a US$13,600 headphone; Rosson publishes neither price nor lead time; a Sennheiser HD 600 is made in Ireland.

stories.headline: Apple opens Singapore orders for a S$6,499 MacBook Pro, resolution unpublished
stories.dek: The first OLED Mac is quoted at 2,000 nits and ten million to one contrast; Apple states no pixel count, no battery capacity and no touch latency.

stories.headline: Glashütte Original launched the Senator Aventurine without publishing a price
stories.dek: Four outlets working from one embargo printed EUR 36,900, EUR 37,800, US$40,400 and A$55,200 — and the maker’s own page says only “price available upon request”.

stories.headline: A24’s Elizabeth Holmes film took first place by US$200,684
stories.dek: “You Can See Everything” made US$10,600,685 across 3,243 cinemas in the third-lowest weekend of 2026 — and the figures are Sunday estimates, with finals due Monday.

stories.kicker: Raising Them Well · Pediatrics On Social Media
stories.headline: No anxiety link in 11,279 twelve-year-olds, Pediatrics reports
stories.dek: Across four annual transitions, problematic social media use predicted depression in two windows at betas of .06 and .07, and anxiety in none — and depression predicted later use just as strongly.

stories.headline: US consumers spent US$113bn more in September, buying no extra goods
stories.dek: Petrol took US$45.7bn of the increase and motor vehicles gave back US$14bn, while real disposable income fell 0.3 per cent in a quarter that grew at a 3.4 per cent annual rate.

stories.headline: Five of ten Singapore tufting studios have closed or paused
stories.dek: The hobby that went viral on video in 2020 is consolidating: a specialist retailer has turned into a general craft shop, and r/Tufting’s second-biggest flair is “Newbie Needing Help”.

stories.headline: A PeerJ meta-analysis puts threshold gains at 38.7 per cent above, 18.4 below
stories.dek: Thirteen studies and 338 people, published 22 October — and the authors report heterogeneity near 89 per cent, meaning the studies substantially disagree.

stories.kicker: The Diary · Two Dates To Put In Print
stories.headline: Tokyo’s Kabukiza opens December sales on 14 November, the basho on 5 December
stories.dek: Japan’s marquee events are closing six to twelve weeks earlier than the guides assume: the Fukuoka sumo tournament is sold out on every one of its fifteen days, with no door sales.
